institution: Royal Conservatoire The Hague (Koninklijk Conservatorium) — Institute of Sonology
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited (Master of Music, University of the Arts The Hague / Hogeschool der Kunsten Den Haag)
language: English — 'The studies will be conducted in English and applicants are expected to be adequately fluent with the language.'
durationEcts: 2 years full-time; 120 ECTS (Dutch Master of Music standard; ECTS not stated on programme page — UNVERIFIED for exact credit total)
whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic music, computer music and sound art. Instruction in composition, live electronic music, field recording, sound installations, algorithmic composition, wave field synthesis, digital sound synthesis, analogue studio techniques, psychoacoustics, spatialisation. Independent research project plus thesis. 'Technology is not merely an adjunct to the existing music practice, but should be used primarily to explore new forms of composition.'
entryRequirements: 'The candidate should have a bachelor's diploma relevant for the professional field of Sonology (composition of electronic and/or acoustic music using fixed media, notation, improvisation or some combination of these, sound synthesis research, sound art, related subjects such as artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering, musicology, music perception, film studies, or as a performing musician).' Plus a two-page study plan: (1) brief description of the proposed master's project (practical and/or theoretical), (2) time planning divided over four semesters, (3) detailed project description with central research question and context, (4) overview of subjects for the final thesis presentation.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. The eligible bachelor list names 'artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering' as relevant fields. A BSc Software Engineering falls squarely inside the stated list. This is one of the very few Field-A masters in Europe that names computer science as a qualifying bachelor.
portfolioSpec: 'Students for the Master of Music in Sonology are selected on the basis of a portfolio with previous compositions, sound installations, recordings of live performances or research results in the form of computer programs, articles, theses, etc.' No number of works, maximum duration or file format is stipulated on the official page — UNVERIFIED (open-ended portfolio).
auditionSpec: 'There is no live admission exam.' Selection is on portfolio + two-page study plan only.
tuitionNonEU: €11,488 per year (institutional tuition fee, Master's programmes, 2026-2027). EEA statutory fee is €2,694. Fees indexed annually.
otherFees: €24 administration fee if paying in 8 instalments. No application or audition fee mentioned.
totalCostEstimate: ≈ €22,976 tuition over 2 years + living costs The Hague (IND requires ~€1,100+/month proof of means) ≈ €26,000–29,000/yr total; ~€52,000–58,000 for the full degree — UNVERIFIED on living-cost figure.
scholarshipName: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship); Excellence Scholarship
scholarships: NL Scholarship: €5,000, one-off, first year only, for non-EEA students. 'It is not possible to apply directly for an NL Scholarship; you will be informed if you have been nominated based on the results of your entrance exam and Master Plan.' Excellence Scholarship: for Master's candidates who perform best in the entrance exams, EEA and non-EEA eligible; amount UNVERIFIED. The two are mutually exclusive. Neither covers full tuition.
englishTest: IELTS minimum 6.0, or TOEFL minimum 80, or TOEIC, or Cambridge English. Non-EU/EEA students must submit proof before 1 September of the entry year.
deadline: 26 February (PRIOR-CYCLE REFERENCE: the 2026 intake deadline was 26 February 2026). For September 2027 entry expect a deadline around late February 2027 — UNVERIFIED, not yet published.
applicationOpens: Applications open after 1 December of the preceding year (for 2026 entry: after 1 December 2025).

UNVERIFIED whether an IND study residence permit can be issued for a non-degree course — this is a critical check for a Tunisian national and must be confirmed with the Royal Conservatoire before relying on this route.

qualification: Master of Music (MMus), Art of Sound
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited (University of the Arts The Hague)
durationEcts: 2 years; 120 ECTS — UNVERIFIED on exact ECTS

auditionSpec: Motivation interview, online via Microsoft Teams, 'max. 30 minutes per candidate', with three jury members, held only if portfolio and Master Project Plan are approved.
totalCostEstimate: ≈ €22,976 tuition + living ≈ €52,000–58,000 total — UNVERIFIED on living costs

deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026 intake): portfolio, Master Project Plan and CV due 26 February 2026; interview invitations notified 31 March 2026; motivation interviews week of 13 April 2026; final admission decision 31 August 2026. Expect the same rhythm for September 2027 — UNVERIFIED.

qualification: Master of Music (MMus) in Composition, or Master of Composition (MComp) [Guildhall Artist]
accreditationStatus: Degrees validated/awarded by Guildhall School of Music & Drama (has UK taught degree-awarding powers)

whatYouStudy: Weekly one-to-one Principal Study lessons in Electronic Music — 'Guildhall is unique in offering one-to-one tuition in Electronic Music' — plus five creative projects and electives. MMus students produce 'three portfolios of musical activity: original artistic output, collaborative projects and project leadership'. Intake restricted to 20 students across the four years of the department.
entryRequirements: 'Applicants should normally have obtained an undergraduate degree with Honours in Music, or international equivalent, as a result of completing a minimum of three years in a music college or university music department.' Guildhall's general academic criterion is an Honours undergraduate degree or international equivalent.
acceptsNonMusic: NO as the stated norm — the academic entry criterion explicitly requires a three-year music-college/university-music-department degree. Guildhall does admit on exceptional artistic merit at audition, but this is not published as an entitlement. UNVERIFIED whether a formal exception route exists for a non-music bachelor.
portfolioSpec: EXACTLY, for postgraduate Electronic & Produced Music applicants: (1) a résumé, CV, EPK or similar document detailing your experience; (2) 'Between 5 and 10 minutes of media examples' of your work; (3) a portfolio commentary explaining context and creative processes. 'Quality, creativity and diversity are more important than length.'
auditionSpec: Two stages after portfolio review. (1) CREATIVE EXERCISE: issued about two weeks before interview — produce 'a piece of music of approximately two minutes in length' on your own equipment within a three-hour window; one week to submit via Dropbox. (2) INTERVIEW: held remotely/online in spring 2027 — discussion of your musical and production background, questions on your creative exercise, and your future professional aspirations. Results issued up to 6 weeks after interview.
tuitionNonEU: £32,410 per year (Overseas, MMus 'All Other Pathways' and MComp, students starting September 2026 onwards). The 2027/28 rate is not yet published — UNVERIFIED, but will be at least this.
otherFees: 'All new Postgraduate International entrants are required to pay a 15% non-refundable deposit of tuition fees' (≈ £4,860). Course-related costs £130–£1,500/yr.
totalCostEstimate: £32,410 tuition + London living £1,300–£1,550/month (Guildhall's own figure) ≈ £48,000–£51,000 for one year. MComp doubles this.
scholarships: Departmental partial scholarships: 'When you have been offered and accepted a place at Guildhall you can apply for a partial scholarship within your department' — amounts and deadlines NOT published; UNVERIFIED. Contact music_applications@gsmd.ac.uk. Chevening is the only realistic full-funding route for a Tunisian and would need to be won separately (deadline 6 Oct 2026).
englishTest: UNVERIFIED — no exact IELTS score published on the pages retrieved.
deadline: CURRENT CYCLE FOR SEPTEMBER 2027 ENTRY: application deadline Tuesday 5 January 2027; portfolio submission deadline 12 January 2027; interviews remote/online in spring 2027.
